text:
morgan: Heads-up — autoscaler didn't reclaim ~6 idle GPU nodes in eu-west1 after the canary finished. Nodes show 0 user pods but CA keeps skipping delete.
suresh: ugh. can you paste 'kubectl describe node' for one of them? also check events for kubelet flaps.
morgan: quick dump: nodes intermittently go NotReady for ~2-4m, then Ready. Also saw local PVs attached (cache-*), but pods already moved to other nodes.
ana: CA won't delete nodes that are NotReady or have local storage depending on flags. what's the cluster-autoscaler args right now?
morgan: posting flags from the helm values:
```
--v=4
--cloud-provider=gcp
--expander=most-pods
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
--scan-interval=30s
--max-empty-bulk-delete=3
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true
--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=true
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
```
suresh: that max-empty-bulk-delete=3 will make bulk reclaiming slow. and skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true + NotReady flaps explains it: CA marks them unsafe.
ana: Agreed. For GPU pools we often flip skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false and reduce scale-down-utilization-threshold to 0.4 so packing is more aggressive, but that can evict cached work. Also consider expander=least-waste so CA prefers nodes with fewer idle GPU capacity.
dave: tradeoffs: turning off skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false can cause CA to delete nodes running critical kube-system pods if they can be rescheduled elsewhere — risky. But our kube-system pods are DaemonSets (nvidia-driver, aws-eni, monitoring) which usually tolerate reschedule. need to check PDBs.
morgan: there are a couple PDBs for stateful infra (prometheus) but not tied to GPU nodepool. driver daemonset is toleration-based. PDBs shouldn't block these specific nodes.
suresh: propose a small rollout: bump max-empty-bulk-delete to 10, set skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false (only for the GPU nodepool autoscaler deployment), change expander to least-waste, lower scale-down-utilization-threshold to 0.45, and keep skip-nodes-with-system-pods=true for safety. also reduce scan-interval to 20s so CA reacts faster.
ana: also add a safeguard: set --node-group-auto-discovery with tags limited to the GPU pool so change doesn't affect CPU pools.
dave: how about kubelet flaps — CA still won't delete if node has recent NotReady. We should tune --scale-down-unready-time (if supported) or ensure node healthcheck window is short. Is the NotReady coming from driver restarts? logs show nv-hostdriver restart 1-2x/day.
morgan: devs are already on a driver fix PR, but we need cost relief immediately.
infra-bot: rollout started: patch cluster-autoscaler in kube-system namespace. CI: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234
suresh: after rollout keep an eye on metric: autoscaler.scale_down.last_deleted_node_count and cost metric in grafana dashboard 'infra/gpu-costs'.
(10m later)
morgan: update — after changing max-empty-bulk-delete=10 and expander=least-waste + skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false, CA removed 4 idle GPU nodes within 7m. No PDB violations, kube-system stable.
dave: nice. Did cost telemetry move?
morgan: overnight cost delta for eu-west GPU pool ~ -7% and average pod scheduling latency unchanged. Will monitor next 48h.
ana: leave a note in runbook: when driver flaps are transient, allow local-storage=false for short window; revert if we see evictions. Also add a dashboard alarm for autoscaler.skip_deletes>5 in 1h.
suresh: I'll open a short RFC for permanent CA flags for GPU pools with pros/cons + rollback plan.
infra-bot: deploy successful: cluster-autoscaler patch applied at 1852002050 by infra-ci
morgan: thanks team :thumbsup:
